title: Decorators
description: Learn about closures and decorators in Python.

sections.title: Functions as Values
sections.markdown: In Python, functions are first-class citizens, meaning they can be passed as functions as values to other functions and returned from them.
key_points: Functions as Values is a core concept to understand
Practice applying Functions in real code

sections.title: What is a Closure?
sections.markdown: A closure occurs when a nested function captures and remembers the variables from its enclosing scope, even after the outer function finishes.
key_points: What is a Closure? is a core concept to understand
Practice applying What in real code

sections.title: What is a Decorator?
sections.markdown: A decorator is a function that takes another function and extends its behavior without explicitly modifying it. It relies on a wrapper function.
key_points: What is a Decorator? is a core concept to understand
Practice applying What in real code

sections.title: Basic Decorator Pattern
sections.markdown: The basic pattern involves an outer function, an inner wrapper function that modifies behavior, and returning the wrapper.
key_points: Basic Decorator Pattern is a core concept to understand
Practice applying Basic in real code

sections.title: Functools Wraps
sections.markdown: Always use `functools.wraps` on the wrapper function to preserve the original function's metadata like its docstring and name.
key_points: Functools Wraps is a core concept to understand
Practice applying Functools in real code

sections.title: Decorators with Arguments
sections.markdown: To pass arguments to a decorator, you need another layer of nesting: a function that takes arguments and returns the actual decorator.
key_points: Decorators with Arguments is a core concept to understand
Practice applying Decorators in real code

sections.title: Stacking Decorators
sections.markdown: Stacking allows multiple decorators on one function. They are applied from bottom to top.
key_points: Stacking Decorators is a core concept to understand
Practice applying Stacking in real code

sections.title: Common Backend Uses
sections.markdown: Some common backend uses of decorators include authentication checks, logging, caching, and rate limiting in web frameworks.
key_points: Common Backend Uses is a core concept to understand
Practice applying Common in real code

sections.title: Class Decorators Awareness
sections.markdown: Besides functions, decorators can also be applied to classes to modify their behavior, such as registering them in a registry.
key_points: Class Decorators Awareness is a core concept to understand
Practice applying Class in real code

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.markdown: Forgetting to return the inner wrapper or not passing `*args, **kwargs` correctly are frequent pitfalls when writing decorators.
key_points: Common Mistakes is a core concept to understand
Practice applying Common in real code

sections.title: Interview Points
sections.markdown: Be ready to write a basic decorator from scratch and explain the role of closures and `functools.wraps` in preserving metadata.
key_points: Interview Points is a core concept to understand
Practice applying Interview in real code
